Jake Ellzey

Republican candidate for U.S. Representative, District 6, Dallas County, Texas · Incumbent

U.S. Representative; retired U.S. Navy pilot

Jake Ellzey is a Republican who has represented Texas's 6th Congressional District in the U.S. House since 2021. He won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 68.4% of the vote, ahead of James Buford and Brian Stahl. He faces Democrat Danny Minton in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Ellzey stands

Election integrity / voter registration
Voted for the SAVE Act in February 2026. The bill would require proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections. He says it strengthens election integrity.
Immigration enforcement
Voted yes on H.Res.488, a resolution thanking ICE for its enforcement operations, and on the Kayla Hamilton Act on immigration detention and enforcement.

Background

  • U.S. Representative, Texas District 6, 2021–present (first elected in a 2021 special election)
  • Texas House of Representatives, District 10, 2021
  • Retired U.S. Navy pilot
  • Member of the House Appropriations Committee
  • Won the 2026 Republican primary with 68.4% (36,175 votes)
